prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Sparse tall row · Server inventory (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Host" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 65px
  col 2: header "Role" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 3: header "Zone" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 79px
  col 4: header "CPU" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 5: header "Status" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 67px
  col 6: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 1403px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Inventory servers by host, role, zone, CPU, status, and operational notes.","reading":"Readers scan hosts and compare roles, locations, CPU counts, and health; the single long note explains an exception and can occupy a taller row.","groups":["Host and Role identify each server and its function.","Zone and CPU describe placement and capacity.","Status and Notes pair health with operational context."],"keep_intact":["Host identifiers where possible","Role names","CPU values","Status words","Zone identifiers where possible"],"may_wrap":["The long operational note at natural word boundaries","Zone identifiers at hyphens if more space is needed for the note"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [86, 80, 100, 53, 88, 312] · table 720×407px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 153, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [86, 80, 100, 48, 88, 317] · table 720×407px · row heights [60, 36, 36, 36, 129, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [86, 80, 78, 53, 88, 334] · table 720×524px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 129, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
